title: The Value of Mandatory Certification: A Real-Effects Perspective

scopes.description: The supplied 799-line online appendix provides analytical equilibrium proofs and six parameterized theoretical figures (OA1-OA6). It includes manual analytical procedures, including a piecewise-profit maximization method for the OA5 audit-market extension, but no executable program, software specification or complete end-to-end plotting recipe. The only packaged author artifact is the appendix PDF.

issues.description: No executable author program is supplied. The appendix contains analytical prose, equations and figure descriptions, but no launchable program or named software workflow.

The appendix provides substantial manual analytical work: equilibrium proofs, parameterized figures OA1-OA6, and a piecewise-profit maximization procedure for the Figure OA5 audit-market extension. It gives no executable calculation or plotting workflow and names no software, so this release cannot be directly run or establish how the plotted panels were produced. References to main-paper results remain context rather than additional input requirements.

evidence.quote:
Online Appendix


OA1          Mandatory Certification but Voluntary Disclosure
Consider another interim regime in which certification is mandatory whereas disclosure is vol-
untary. Specifically, F has no other options but has to always disclose and certify all received
evidence; S can choose whether or not to disclose, but upon disclosure, the evidence must be cer-
tified. All other model setups are developed in the same way as in the main model. The following
lemma summarizes the equilibrium in this interim regime.

evidence.description: The appendix gives an analytical maximization procedure for the mandatory-disclosure fee by comparing region-edge profits.
evidence.quote:

   We first discuss the determination of the optimal certification fee fM D in the mandatory dis-
closure regime. We observe that the sub-profit-function in each region is increasing in f and thus
the local maximum profit lies at the right edge of each region of f . Note that strictly speaking,
in the regions (c, c̄M D ) and [c̄M D , V − 1), the locally optimal certification fees are respectively
c̄M D − ε and V − 1 − ε, where ε > 0 is close to zero. To simplify analysis and exposition, we
treat all sub-sets right-closed. As such, to determine the global maximum profit, we only need
to compare the three local maximum profits; that is, the global maximum profit for the certifier
